rationale.conceptual: Applying GGA-PW91 DFT and CI-NEB to study adsorption/dissociation is an established method; setting up pseudopotentials, k-points, and slab models demands non-trivial understanding but no new theory.
rationale.execution: Multi-stage pipeline (~5 phases: relax slabs, reference energies, physisorption relaxations with multiple orientations, chemisorption site testing, two NEB calculations) with dependencies and tool installation; moderately complex but scriptable.

difficulty.reasoning: The task reproduces standard DFT-based adsorption and NEB barrier calculations on small graphene slabs, requiring careful parameter setup and multi-step workflow but no novel algorithms.

compute_estimate.reasoning: Small 4×4 graphene slabs (32 atoms) with plane-wave DFT; calculations are CPU-bound, memory ~8 GB, pseudopotential files are tiny, no large datasets.
